item.title: Willie Fritz on expanded College Football Playoff and Cougars' chances this year | UH football notes
item.description: Houston Cougars fans celebrate after wide receiver Amare Thomas' 8-yard touchdown catch during an NCAA college football game in Houston, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) University of Houston coach Willie Fritz said Monday that he supports the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, saying the new format will give more programs access to the postseason. The CFP will double in size beginning in 2027, part of a five-year deal between ESPN and the CFP announced Monday, while also eliminating Power Four conference championship games. "I think it gives more people access," Fritz said at his weekly press conference to preview Friday's game at Colorado. "I think people are thirsty for college football and quality games, and that will certainly give you more." BOHLS: Expansion to 24 teams is wrong, greedy and bad for sport The 24-team field will include 19 at-large bids, the Power Four champions as determined by each league, plus the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Big 12 announced Monday that this year's conference championship game, Dec. 4 in Arlington, will be its last. Beginning next year, the regular-season champion will receive the Big 12's automatic bid. In a 24-team field, UH - which was No. 17 in the first CFP rankings - would be in good position to receive an at-large bid and be in position to host a first-round game on campus. REACTION: What coaches are saying The Cougars are still in the hunt for this season's 12-team field, needing to win their final three games and have Texas Tech lose once. In that scenario, UH would win most of the tiebreakers involving multiple two-loss teams and advance to the Big 12 championship game. The Cougars' current CFP ranking is the highest in program history. "You want to be relevant," Fritz said. "We certainly want Houston to be out there front and center as much as possible. So that's great. But you've got to finish the year, and you've got to keep playing well. Being ranked right now doesn't mean a whole lot. You want to be ranked as high as we can at the end of the season. That means we've accomplished some things." A positive return Linebacker Jaden Yates had a team-high nine tackles Saturday after missing a month with a lower-body injury. Yates suffered the injury in Week 5 against UCF and missed the next three games before returning after the open week. "I thought he did a good job," Fritz said. "He doesn't seem to have any side effects from the injury. There are a lot of things that he does for us back there." Yates has the green dot on the back of his helmet, which signifies he is equipped with a coach-to-player radio communication system. Part of Yates' responsibility is to relay instructions from defensive coordinator Austin Armstrong to the rest of the unit and help with alignment. When he was out, that responsibility fell to Sione Fotu and Carmycah Glass. "I think (Yates) knocked a lot of the rust off and will play even better this week," Fritz said.

item.title: Manchester United coach Michael Carrick ‘expected’ to be fired after rough start
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Manchester United coach Michael Carrick ‘expected’ to be fired after rough start appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Currently in the Premier League’s relegation zone, Manchester United have won just one league game so far this season. Their eight points put them above Sunderland on goal difference alone, while both clubs are only one point ahead of last-place Crystal Palace. After saving the Red Devils in an interim role last year, head coach Michael Carrick had the label removed after the club’s finish following former manager Ruben Amorim’s firing. Now, it appears that Carrick could be joining him. According to The Athletic’s David Ornstein, Adam Crafton, and Laurie Whitwell, Manchester United is expected to fire Carrick before this current international break ends. “Manchester United are expected to relieve Michael Carrick of his duties as head coach,” wrote the trio on Monday afternoon. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) United’s 1-5-4 record and -5 goal differential are just the start of the club’s woes so far this fall. Following another busy summer transfer window in which the Red Devils’ midfield was rebuilt with three signings, expectations were high at Old Trafford. Many believed that Manchester United would not only challenge for the Premier League title, but once again compete in European football as well. However, Carrick has failed to deliver on those goals. Manchester United has only beaten Ipswich Town at home in the Premier League, and that was on August 30th. They’ve only won two of their four Champions League matchups, most recently against Roma at home last week. A home victory over Sabah on September 10th is the only other victory for the Red Devils this fall. After a disappointing start filled with heartbreak and questionable decision making, it makes sense that the Manchester United brass would look to make a change. Owners Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer Family, along with other key team leaders like team CEO Omar Berrada, will make the ultimate call on Carrick’s future over the current international break. By the time that United return to the pitch on November 22nd against Liverpool at Anfield, a new head coach could be roaming the visiting sidelines. Will Carrick’s potential replacement lead Manchester United back to the promised land? Or will it be another failed appointment, like Carrick, Amorim and Erik ten Hag were over the last three years? item.title: Why I believe Carson Benge should have won NL Rookie of the Year
item.description: The Major League Baseball season's characterization as a "marathon" is more appropriate than any other professional sport. There are plenty of ebbs and flows over the course of the 162-game season. Performances can't be defined by a single month or stretch of time. The extensive nature of the campaign is what made the National League race for Rookie of the Year one of the most contentious contests in the MLB Award season. Over the course of six months, five candidates rose to the top in the Reds' Sal Stewart, Mets' Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt and Rockies' TJ Rumfield. In the end, it was Stewart who was named the NL Rookie of the Year honor as the Baseball Writers Association of American announced the award on Monday night. Stewart took home the honor on the strength of his 32 home runs and 112 RBI, which led all NL rookies, along with 87 runs, a .787 OPS, 25 doubles and 15 stolen bases. Stewart earned 20 of the 30 possible first-place votes. The Mets' Benge ended up as the runner-up with seven first-place votes, three second-place votes and 12 third-place designations. One of those votes for Benge to receive the top honor was mine. When the BBWAA assigned its award designations to the writers in early August, the Rookie of the Year race appeared to be a two-horse race between Stewart and Wetherholt. But over the the final two months of the season, Benge's kick provided further intrigue. That's why the season is a marathon. And by the completion of the 2026 season, I believe Benge had done enough in all facets of the game to warrant the top slot in the Rookie of the Year vote. Stewart's explosive bat made him a top contender. The Reds first baseman had the second-most RBI and eighth-most home runs in the National League while he slashed .263/.330/.457. Wetherholt proved he had one of the best gloves in all of baseball, boasting a +25 outs above average that trailed only Cubs MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong for the best mark in baseball. While batting atop the Cardinals' lineup, the second baseman led all rookies with 89 runs, while adding 17 home runs, 51 RBI and 14 stolen bases but posting an unassuming .242/.339/.365 slash line in 139 games. Benge provided the best of both worlds in terms of offense and defense despite a slow start through the opening two months, which hurt his case in the early going. The Mets right-fielder led all rookies with 168 hits — matching the Tigers' Kevin McGonigle in the American League — and was second among NL rookies in batting average (.282) and home runs (20) and third in RBI (65) and stolen bases (22). Benge is the only NL rookie to finish in the top three in each of those key offensive categories. Most of that production came after Benge opened with a .189 batting average and .525 OPS through the month of April. He slashed .299/.363/.457 over the final five months. item.title: Vikings-Bills live discussion: A chaotic matchup between a pair of overrated teams
item.description: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-1 Buffalo Bills take on the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. These are two of the best teams in the NFL record-wise, but they are from the most complete teams. The Vikings’ offense has been asleep at the wheel all season. Justin Jefferson is on pace for a career worst year. He won’t have Kyler Murray throwing him the ball tonight, but that might be a blessing in disguise, as Murray tends to be erratic and miss open receivers downfield. What Minnesota lacks offensively, they more than make up for it on the defensive side of the ball. They are comfortably the best stop unit in the league, thanks in large part to their ability to prevent success against the pass. Brian Flores blitzes over 3/4 of the time, and invites chaotic play. If there’s a quarterback who thrives in chaos, it’s Josh Allen. Allen makes play after play, usually off-script. He’s down left tackle Dion Dawkins, which might invite Allen to run more. I can see Allen and James Cook having big days on the ground, and Khalil Shakir pitching in on key third downs. The Bills are lousy defensively. They’ve allowed 33, 31, 29, 34, and 30 points this season. So, if there was a get-right spot for Carson Wentz, Jefferson, and the Vikings, it’s the Bills’ defense that gave up 30 points to the Raiders team we just watched. My gut says the NFC’s strength tops the AFC’s in this game, and the Vikings eke out a win. But going against Allen is asking for it. Deep down, I think these are two overrated teams that’ll be exposed come playoff time.

item.title: Sal Stewart named NL Rookie of the Year
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MAY 27: Sal Stewart #27 of the Cincinnati Reds in action against the New York Mets at Citi Field on May 27, 2026 in New York City. The Mets defeated the Reds 4-2. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Reds first baseman Sal Stewart has been named NL Rookie of the Year, taking home 20 of 30 first place votes en route to a comfortable win. Stewart takes home the award on the back of a .263/.330/.457 season (112 wRC+) with 32 HR and 112 RBI, with 15 steals tacked on to boot. Carson Benge finished second, while Nolan McLean finished 4th. Benge was named a finalist for the award alongside JJ Wetherholdt and Stewart last week. Thomas Henderson profiled each of those finalists earlier today , concluding that Stewart was the likeliest to win on the back of his 30 homer season. Indeed, Stewart has already been named Sporting News Rookie of the Year , a version of award voted on by players rather than writers. Earlier today ahead of the official announcement, betting odds (per Kalshi) had Stewart as a shoe-in for the official version of the award. While it’s easy to understand why Stewart has supporters (Dingerz, baby), his analytical case is quite poor. Wetherholdt and Benge were both far superior players by all WAR metrics, and even other rookies like TJ Rumfield and Joe Mack were more valuable overall contributors. A.J. Ewing, who tallied only 492 AB to Stewarts’s 700, was nearly as valuable in his own right. At least three rookies on the mound – Logan Henderson, Andrew Alvarez, and Nolan McLean – were also more valuable players. In prior years, this would’ve been a mild annoyance to debate in chat threads or on Twitter, but with the implementation of the Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI) system there are actual stakes here. For the Mets, this is a frustrating and somewhat damaging outcome. Despite having two of the three best rookies in Benge and McLean, the org will not receive anything in the way of draft pick awards, a boon that would’ve greatly helped their eternally challenged draft pool.

item.title: Michael Carrick on the brink at Manchester United amid club review
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United manager Michael Carrick applauds the fans after the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Michael Carrick on the brink at Manchester United amid club review») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United head coach appear to be numbered as the club reviews his position and considers alternatives. The Red Devils will spend the international break in the relegation zone after failing to add to August's solitary Premier League win against Ipswich in Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. United languish in 18th spot and are reviewing Carrick's position as the club take stock during the international break, the Press Association understands. Reports suggest the club intend to replace the former midfielder following talks on Monday, although Old Trafford sources insisted no decision had been made that evening. United director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada seriously considered sacking Carrick a fortnight ago after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth compounded a calamitous 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. The club eventually decided to give the head coach and his players the opportunity to turn the situation around before the international break. Carrick's side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday's 3-2 comeback win against Roma and Sunday's 4-4 draw with Villa. United have been considering whether that run merits him staying on and would have to push a manager who headed into the international break having stressed he would not walk away. Asked if the November pause comes at a good time for the group, the under-fire United boss said: "Yeah, it's been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you're looking at the events. "But I'm pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there. "Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so. "But as a normal international week is, you know, we'll have some training. We'll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we'll train, and we'll get ready for the next game." The final international break of the year would seem a logical time if United wanted to make a change, given there is no free midweek until mid-December after returning with a trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22. Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann are contenders to replace Carrick if the club decide a change in the Old Trafford hotseat is necessary. item.description: The Denver Broncos just keep on finding ways to win . On Sunday, Bo Nix and company stretched their winning streak to five games after taking down the Carolina Panthers in another thriller, 26-21. His mother grew up in the Bay Area, just like Brady, and their families apparently knew each other through his grandfather, who had played with Brady’s father. item.title: Army-Navy game moves up a week to accommodate expanded CFP
item.description: Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images One second-order effect of the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams is the annual Army-Navy game, which has traditionally been held on the second weekend of December, following conference championship weekend. With ESPN and the CFP officially announcing the expansion to 24 teams on Monday, the Army-Navy game also officially got its new date. Next year’s Army-Navy game will be played on Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, one week earlier than the originally scheduled date of Dec. 11. The game, which is broadcast annually by CBS, will now be played the week following rivalry week, which is the last official week of the regular season. Army-Navy will now occupy the Saturday that used to be reserved for a full slate of conference championship games. The Army-Navy Game announced today that the 2027 Army-Navy Game presented by USAA, the 128th playing of America’s Game, will be played Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. The date change from Dec. 11 was necessitated by the CFP moving to 24 teams and starting on Dec. 9. → https://t.co/lCIx6Pbqmp #ArmyNavy — Army-Navy Game (@ArmyNavyGame) November 9, 2026 Where to put the Army-Navy game in an expanded CFP format was often a footnote in discussions about potential expansion until President Trump signed an executive order earlier this year mandating that the annual matchup between the two service academies have its own standalone time slot, free of any other FBS games. Moving the game to the first weekend of December should allow for that, as conference championship games will no longer occupy those television windows. “We are thankful to the city of Philadelphia and Lincoln Financial Field for their efforts to manage the date change of the 2027 Army-Navy Game to ensure the Game is played in its exclusive time slot on CBS,” Tom Theodorakis, director of athletics and chief executive officer of Army West Point Athletic Association, said in an announcement . “As we look ahead to future games, we are excited about the opportunity to build on our strong foundation and secure new commitments that demonstrate a shared passion to grow the game and drive economic impact in host cities.” “We appreciate the flexibility of the people of Philadelphia to accommodate this date change, and we applaud the collaboration between the city of Philadelphia, Lincoln Financial Field and the academies,” Michael Kelly, Director of Athletics of the Naval Academy and President of the Naval Academy Athletic Association, said in Monday’s release. “We are also extremely grateful to the CFP leadership for their collaboration. Finding a way to preserve the exclusive broadcast window for America’s Game while ensuring our program has a rightful path to compete in the College Football Playoff is a tremendous outcome for our student-athletes and fans across the country.” The post Army-Navy game moves up a week to accommodate expanded CFP appeared first

item.description: Sheesh. Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) touched down in Scotland for the first time this past weekend (Sat., Nov. 7, 2026), staging BKFC 96 inside the sold-out OVO Hydro in Glasgow. In the main event, Sean Weir captured the vacant BKFC U.K. Light Heavyweight championship by stopping Leigh Cohoon in the first round ( watch highlights here ). However, the second fight on the BKFC 96 main card produced the most chilling highlight of the night. Cory Chapman needed just 40 seconds to brutally knock out Lewis Dixon in their Bantamweight showdown. item.title: Mariners look forward and back in current coaching staff hires
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 04: New manager Jason Kanzler #18 of the Seattle Mariners poses for the camera during a photoshoot at T-Mobile Park on November 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Ben VanHouten/Seattle Mariners/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Mariners made the hires of bench coach Tanner Swanson and hitting coach CJ Gillman official today, continuing a theme that started when the hiring of manager Jason Kanzler was officially announced last week: the youth movement is coming back to Seattle. In Dipoto’s first season, the Mariners trended towards conservative hires or retaining coaches who had already been in the organization. Dipoto brought over several people he’d worked with during his time with the Angels – Mike Micucci, Ethan Katz, and Zac Livingston – and retained most other staff members rather than cleaning house organizationally from top to bottom. But by 2016, Dipoto and then-Director of Player Development Andy McKay were ready to take some bigger swings. One of the biggest was hiring a 32-year-old Mitch Canham to manage their A-ball affiliate, the Clinton LumberKings. At the time, Canham was well-known to Northwest baseball fans as a standout star at Lake Stevens high school and then Oregon State, but an unknown quantity in the broader coaching world, lacking any official managerial experience before being handed the reins at a full-season affiliate. Canham’s hiring was part of an organizational philosophy shift that emphasized quality of leadership over depth of experience – as McKay put it, “ better people make better baseball players ”, which starts with them being led by the best people available. Joining Canham in Clinton was pitching coach Pete Woodworth, who had more official coaching experience but was just 28 years old at the time. Those hires sparked an influx of young coaching talent, often from non-traditional coaching backgrounds, into the Mariners organization. The next few years would see the hiring of at the time relatively unknown names, many of whom who have since moved on from Seattle to build impressive coaching resumes elsewhere: Tony Arnerich, Carson Vitale, Hugh Quattlebaum, Max Weiner, Jarret DeHart, Rob Marcello, Sean McGrath, just to name a handful. Those coaches oversaw the transition of the Mariners farm system from one of the worst in baseball to a consistent solid performer, and the pitching coaches especially helped the Mariners earn a well-deserved reputation as one of the sport’s best in developing pitchers. But the Mariners paid the price – or rather, didn’t – for that innovation, losing many of their young coaches to better opportunities (and/or better salaries) elsewhere. Two that stung the most were the losses of Canham and Weiner, both of whom moved on to high-profile (and high-paid) jobs at the college level. The Eagles signed Davis to a three-year, $78 million extension in March after he had a breakout 2025 season. The 2-7 Eagles sent a clear message to the rest of the NFL with this blockbuster move: They are rebuilding and could be open to trading star players for the right price. The Eagles were expected to make minor moves, such as trading players on expiring contracts. But the Davis trade changes the thinking. The Eagles could be tempted to trade another star player if they can land more first- and second-round picks. The Eagles now possess two 2027 first-round picks and two 2028 first-round picks. They also have two second-round picks in 2028 and 2029. The Eagles have the ammunition to build another Super Bowl contender. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are holed up in cozy U.S. Bank Stadium and ready for a primetime showdown with the Minnesota Vikings under the spectacle that is Monday Night Football . Tonight, it’s a showdown between two 6-1 teams with vastly different roads to success in 2026. The Bills and their league-best scoring offense are of course led by quarterback Josh Allen while featuring one of the most lethal rushing attacks directed by running back James Cook III. Where they’ve struggled is on defense, and against opponents’ passing attacks. Is that a recipe for disaster this evening with wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison set to play catch with quarterback Carson Wentz? Well, expect Jefferson and Addison to get plenty of chances to see how they fare against cornerbacks Christian Benford and rookie Davison Igbinosun. Tonight does present a massive challenge for Buffalo’s offense. Allen will have an entirely new pair of offensive linemen protecting him on the left side — and against a ferocious Vikings pass rush. It’s not an ideal situation, to be clear, having a starting pair in left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson sidelined for this game . In their place will be offensive tackle Tylan Grable, and offensive guard Austin Corbett. No pressure, right? It’s time to find out what the next men up have up their sleeve to take on the NFL’s best and stingiest defense, a Vikings unit that blitzes as though their life depended upon it. It’s likely we see head coach Joe Brady call a lot of early runs and quick passes to both wear the defense down and allow Allen to settle into rhythm. Winning in the NFL is tough, and this might be the Bills’ biggest challenge yet. Though you may be looking for Allen and company to air it out, and expect Buffalo’s defense to continue an upward trajectory based off last week’s thrashing of the Baltimore Ravens, a win is a win, signature or otherwise. Remember, for those of you without cable or streaming service options, the ESPN broadcast is also shown live on your local ABC station. After a second hearing in which Sane and head coach Rick Pitino testified, the Queens Supreme Court couldn’t reach a decision on the St. John’s forward’s lawsuit against the NCAA. Justice Karina E. Alomar requested a memorandum of law from both sides due by Tuesday, November 30, according to Zach Braziller. Although Sane agreed to the contract, his attorney argues he did not compete, train, or attend training camp with the NBA team. Sane signed with St. John’s after spending the last five years playing in the NBA G-League and other professional leagues in Europe and Africa, most recently putting up 9.9 points and 3.8 rebounds on 46.7% shooting with German club MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg last season.
